cluster_thesis.text: Two legs on different clocks. The hyperscaler leg is mid-to-late: 2026 capex of $660-690B across MSFT/GOOG/AMZN/META/ORCL is already guided, so the incremental surprise is now cost and FCF, not volume. The neocloud leg is early and its financing model has never been tested through a full rate cycle -- with the 10-yr +12.4bp over a month and a hawkish cached Fed, cost of capital is the transmission channel and it touches only NBIS and IREN. Cluster sits on its 10% policy floor with $3,626 of ceiling room, so the honest question is which leg gets the room, not whether to hold.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: Any of MSFT/GOOG/AMZN/META guiding 2027 capex flat-to-down, or any neocloud failing to place a GPU-backed facility at spread, breaks this read.

margin_pool.moving_toward: Contracted-offtake neoclouds with named investment-grade counterparties, and hyperscalers owning in-house silicon -- plus the vendors taking equity/vendor-financing positions rather than pure sales (NVDA into IREN).
margin_pool.moving_away_from: Speculative-capacity neoclouds funded by convertibles and GPU collateral, where financing cost is compounding faster than revenue.

evidence.claim: CoreWeave Q2 2026 net interest expense $640M vs $267M a year earlier -- interest +140% against revenue +112%; when financing cost outgrows revenue the margin migrates from the renter to the lender
FY26 free cash flow expected to go near zero or negative for all major hyperscalers except Alphabet and Microsoft, on collective 2026 capex of $660-690B
evidence.source: FactSet Insight, Hyperscalers Tap External Financing as AI Capex Outruns Cash Flow

evidence.claim: NVIDIA signed a $3.4B five-year cloud deal with IREN and pledged up to $2.1B of investment -- acting as supplier and capital partner at once

differentiator_reads.read: One of only two majors (with Alphabet) whose FY26 FCF stays positive after ~$190B of 2026 capex; everyone else goes to zero or negative

differentiator_reads.axis: cloud revenue growth vs capex growth
differentiator_reads.read: Signed a $9.7B contract with IREN -- it can rent capacity instead of owning it, which is capex optionality no other member has and caps the capex/revenue gap on the downside

ranking.case_against: Thesis status is `watch` and marked unverified; capex/OCF is still rising, and the OpenAI-linked commitments are the least disclosed line in the guide. ATR 1.95% means it also captures the least of the tailwind on the upside.

differentiator_reads.read: Blue Owl-led $2.4B compute-equipment financing plus NVDA up to $2.1B pledged -- vendor- and asset-anchored rather than dilutive

differentiator_reads.axis: customer contract duration and counterparty quality
differentiator_reads.read: NVDA $3.4B five-year deal and a $9.7B Microsoft contract -- named investment-grade counterparties, multi-year duration; $4B contracted FY26 ARR capacity

ranking.case_against: FY27 capex guide of $25-30B against a $17.6B market cap is a financing requirement, not a plan, and it lands into a rising-10-yr, rising-AI-credit-CDS regime. Large net loss, ATR 8.05%, and this is the book's third entry after two prior stop-outs -- a documented repeat-volatility pattern.

differentiator_reads.axis: neocloud financing structure: debt, GPU collateral, contracted vs speculative
differentiator_reads.read: $5B convertible note priced and closed -- convert-and-dilute funding, and the stock fell 14% on 08-19 on exactly that concern; contrast IREN's vendor/asset-anchored structure

differentiator_reads.axis: customer contract duration and counterparty quality
differentiator_reads.read: Four AI cloud deals averaging >$1B TCV each, but counterparties are undisclosed -- contract quality is unassessable, which is itself the finding versus IREN naming NVDA and MSFT

ranking.case_against: Case FOR, which is mandatory here: Q2 revenue +454% YoY to $582M and over $9B of expected 2026 customer prepayments. Prepayments are the highest-quality funding in the neocloud stack -- better than debt or converts -- and if NBIS names those four counterparties it moves up this ladder quickly. Held back operationally by undisclosed Vineland data-centre issues, and it is over its risk cap (1.47x, -$501 headroom, rotation_bucket trim_risk_cap) at ATR 9.88%.

reorder_when: By 2026-10-21 (GOOG Q3): if Alphabet raises 2027 capex again while cloud revenue growth decelerates, GOOG drops below IREN -- self-funding stops being a virtue when the spend has no revenue answer.
If NBIS discloses the counterparties on its four ~$1B TCV deals and any are investment-grade, NBIS and IREN swap on the counterparty-quality axis.
If the 09-15/16 FOMC delivers a hawkish hold and the 10-yr adds another 15bp+, both neoclouds drop below both hyperscalers regardless of contract news -- cost of capital dominates ranks 3-4.
If MSFT's next capex guide converts more of its build into third-party rental, MSFT's lead widens; if it re-internalises, MSFT loses its optionality edge over GOOG.
Any change to depreciation useful-life assumptions at MSFT or GOOG disclosed in the 10-Q reorders ranks 1-2 on earnings quality.

redundant_pairs.same_bet_because: Both are GPU neoclouds whose equity is a levered call on the same AI-rental demand, both dependent on external financing (converts, GPU collateral, vendor capital), and both repriced by the same move in rates and AI-credit spreads -- a single CPI or FOMC print moves them together. But the financing STRUCTURE differs materially (vendor/asset-anchored vs convert-and-dilute) and counterparty disclosure differs, so they are not interchangeable.

bench.entry_condition: Only after CRWV shows net interest expense growing slower than revenue for one quarter (it was +140% vs +112% in Q2 2026) -- and not before the 09-15/16 FOMC. A $104B contracted backlog against a ~$49-59B market cap with named counterparties, versus NBIS's undisclosed four deals.

Enter on a Q3 guide that holds capex flat or shows AWS growth accelerating faster than capex; ATR 2.13% makes it the low-volatility way to use the cluster's floor room. ~$200B of 2026 capex funded from operating cash flow with an in-house accelerator and no dilution.

Enter only if the 2027 capex guide is accompanied by a disclosed revenue-per-dollar-of-capex metric; without it this is spend without an answer. Pure AI-capex demand with no counterparty or refinancing risk.
Wants a print showing RPO conversion to revenue; FCF is expected negative in FY26, so entry needs the financing plan disclosed first. OCI is a contracted-RPO business with disclosed mega-customers.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision (09-15/16) -- neocloud cost of capital is the transmission channel; near-zero direct read to MSFT/GOOG
Alphabet Q3 print and 2027 capex guide -- the apex read-through: any hyperscaler capex guide moves all 95.4% of this book, not just this cluster
MSFT / AMZN / META fiscal-quarter prints with FY27 capex framing
Any CoreWeave financing round or GPU-backed facility pricing -- reprices the whole neocloud sub-group's cost of capital, not just the issuer

thesis_tensions.tension: Ranked leader of the cluster on a `watch` thesis whose evidence_against array is empty and which is marked verified=unverified. Either the thesis under-rates a name that is one of only two self-funding hyperscalers, or my rank over-rates it because the axes I can evidence (FCF after capex, rental optionality) are exactly the ones a `watch` on OpenAI-commitment disclosure would not show up in.

The only `strengthening` name in the cluster ranks second, not first, and carries an RSI of 28.9 -- the weakest technical position here. A strengthening thesis and an oversold tape usually mean opportunity, but with no cached 1-month return I could not confirm the de-rate is still live.

No tension on status, but a sizing tension: the cluster laggard is also the largest position in the cluster (3.97% weight, $1,572) and is over its risk cap at 1.47x with rotation_bucket trim_risk_cap. The book's biggest hyperscaler-cluster bet is on its lowest-ranked member.
